conceptual assets.information: The per-channel enable state determines whether PWM counting and waveform generation operate and contributes to the aggregate clock-generation enable. It is written through the bus and can be returned in the configuration read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: a bus write asserted through we_i updates the enable state at lines 183-184, with the write path supplied from the request at lines 99-110. Availability: the enable state clears or stops the counters and PWM operation at lines 212-225 and drives clkgen_en_o at line 197, so it can disable channel operation.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue an unchecked channel configuration write that clears the enable bit, disabling PWM operation and the clock-generation request through lines 183-184 and 197.

conceptual assets.information: The prescaler selection and clock-divider limit determine the tick rate and therefore the timing and period of each PWM channel. The settings are written through the bus and included in configuration read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: bus writes can modify the prescaler and divider settings at lines 183, 185 and 187. Availability: the settings select the timing source and determine whether divider ticks occur at lines 214-219, so an attacker can select a missing or excessively slow tick rate and withhold useful PWM activity.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write a timing configuration that selects an unsuitable clock-generator bit or a very large divider, making PWM updates effectively stall through lines 214-219.

conceptual assets.information: The duty-cycle setting determines how many timer ticks in a PWM period produce the active waveform level. It is stored per channel and is returned through the configuration read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: a bus configuration write stores wdata_i(7 downto 0) into the duty setting at lines 183 and 188, and the setting controls the PWM comparison at line 231.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could overwrite the duty-cycle field through a bus write, causing the PWM output to have an incorrect duty cycle at lines 188 and 231-234.

conceptual assets.information: The polarity setting determines which logical level represents the active portion of the PWM waveform. It is stored per channel, affects the generated output, and is returned through configuration read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: a bus configuration write stores the polarity bit at lines 183 and 186, and the stored value or its inverse is assigned to the PWM output at lines 231-234.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could overwrite the polarity bit through the configuration write path, inverting the intended PWM waveform at lines 186 and 232-234.

conceptual assets.information: The decoded bus address selects which repeated PWM channel receives a read or write access. This routing decision is needed to program or read the intended channel and has no direct output-port representation because it only controls internal channel access.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: the address comparison produces the channel-selection decision at line 109, which controls the per-channel write and read enables at lines 110-111 and can therefore redirect a configuration access.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter bus_req_i.addr so that a valid configuration write is routed to a different PWM channel through lines 109-111.

conceptual assets.information: The generated multi-channel PWM waveform is the primary functional output used by the integrating design for timed control signals. It has no entry port because it is generated internally from the stored configuration and counters.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: the waveform is produced from the enable, polarity, duty setting and duty counter at lines 231-234, all of which can be changed through configuration writes at lines 183-188. Availability: clearing the enable state resets the counters and forces a constant output at lines 212-225 and 231-234, preventing normal PWM activity.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could modify the channel configuration so that the required PWM waveform is inverted, mistimed or replaced by a constant level through lines 231-234.
